title: Lord Gwyn's Firstborn
snippet:
Long ago, the Nameless King was a god of war and heir to lightning. The firstborn was a god of war, and inherited sunlight, which manifests as lightning.
The Nameless King wielded the Dragonslayer Swordspear, a weapon from the Age of Gods. The firstborn similarly wielded a great spear.
The firstborn eventually committed a grave error in the eyes of Anor Londo, which led to the rescinding of his deific status and his removal from the annals of history, his name forgotten. The Nameless King sacrificed everything to ally with the ancient dragons, whom he once fought.
The Nameless King wore a crown and bracelets that greatly resemble those once worn by Gwyn, the First Lord.
Dragon Slayer Ornstein, once the faithful first knight of the Sun's firstborn, left Anor Londo in the dragonless age in search of the Nameless King. His weapon, a cross spear, is extremely similar to that wielded by the Nameless King.

Gwyn's firstborn preserved his father's design and instructions, shepherding humans on the path to the Linking of the First Flame to continue the Age of Fire. In fact, underneath Anor Londo, a city was built exclusively for the undead, with an altar inside for the firstborn of Gwyn, and the aim of guiding a chosen undead who would one day sacrifice themselves to the Flame. Inside the city was the Undead Parish, a church at the center of the cult of the burg and connected to the first test to start on the path of Firelinking and ring the first Bell of Awakening. title: The Nameless King
snippet:
The Nameless King -  Dark Souls III - boss - theories 
 theories : It is possible to theorize that the name of Gwyn's firstborn was "Gwyn-**Sen**" (セン).
**Before linking the First Flame, Lord Gwyn had entrusted his "male children" with the task of shepherding humans into following his example, through the prophecy of the Chosen Undead. The Undead Burg was likely built under the reign of the firstborn, as a statue of him can be found near the Undead Parish. Consequently, it is possible to theorize that Sen's Fortress, created as a proving ground to access Anor Londo and obtain the Lordvessel, all steps required as proofs of the prophecy, was also created by the firstborn, thereby making its name "Sen's Fortress"(センの古城). The particle "Gwyn" before the name comes from the fact that Gwyn's other children, known and openly recognized as legitimate, carry it in their name like "Gwyn-evere" and "Gwyn-dolin".

title: The Nameless King
snippet: It is possible to theorize that Faraam is the name that the people of Forossa used in veneration of Gwyn's firstborn after his name was lost over the centuries. Not only does Faraam share with the Nameless King the title of "god of war", but the god was also able to bless the armor of Forossa Knights, whose helmet depicted a knight fighting an enormous dragon, implying that Faraam was not a "false" deity created by the legends of men but an active entity in the kingdom who was capable of performing the miracles of the ancient gods. The Lion Knights of Forossa, besides bearing the title "Lion" same as Gwyn's firstborn and first knight, were not only mighty but rabid warriors obsessed with fighting; Forossan knights knew only war and no other ways of living, to the point that they didn't even know what they were fighting for, similarly to the Nameless King who "had respect only for arms, and nothing else".

title: The Nameless King
snippet: The eldest son of Gwyn eventually decided to "sacrifice everything" to ally himself with the dragons. In the eyes of the other deities of Anor Londo, archenemies of the dragons, his actions amounted to an unforgivable sin; he was therefore dethroned and exiled from the city. The former king was deprived of his deific status, his statues destroyed and his name erased from the annals of history. Before leaving Anor Londo, the eldest left his sunlight blade miracle and ring on Gwyn's empty tomb in his mausoleum as a final farewell, still paying respects for his father. Now excommunicated from the pantheon of the gods and without a home, the god of war continued to watch closely over his warriors of the sunlight, listening to their prayers and rewarding the proofs of their exploits with his miracles of Sunlight Spear and Great Lightning Spear.

title: Archdragon Peak
snippet:
Archdragon Peak can be entered only after learning the Path of the Dragon gesture found upon a corpse of a Drakeblood Knight in the Consumed King's Garden; this faction of knights can be summoned in Archdragon Peak by the man serpents there. Drakeblood Knights worshiped the blood of dragons; and the red cloth decorating their armor is said to symbolize their yearning for blood.

In Archdragon Peak, the Calamity Ring is found, reportedly made from the orange eye of a calamitous dragon, the ring considered a symbol of dragon worship. This dragon was none other than Black Dragon Kalameet, said to be the last one of ancient dragons.

The Nameless King, known for once allying with ancient dragons, resides on Archdragon Peak. He is accompanied by a stormdrake, which he tamed and fought alongside him. Dragon Slayer Ornstein's weapon and armor can be found laying around the Nameless King's arena; he was said to have left his guard in Anor Londo cathedral to search for the Nameless King.

snippet: The Falconers, a group of mercenaries hired to protect the elites of Volgen, were still part of the covenant of those that worshipped the God of the Sun and possessed their Sunlight Medals. title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: After his father Gwyn linked the First Flame, his throne passed to his firstborn son who, treacherously, chose to "ally" with the ancient dragons, the ancient enemies of the gods, and was therefore dethroned, exiled and his name eradicated from history. Following these events, his sister Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight abandoned Anor Londo together with nearly all of the other deities, leaving Gwyndolin as the last remaining deity in the city. Despite being the last son of the royal family of the gods, Gwyndolin was psychologically unfit to become the next ruler, still playing the feminine role imposed on him by his father Gwyn, leaving Lloyd to take advantage of the situation who proclaimed himself king of the gods, justified by his being Gwyn's uncle, and become the chief deity of the Way of White.

title: The Nameless King
snippet: In the heyday of Lothric, when the descendants of Drangleic and followers of the Way of Blue and the Heirs of the Sun moved to another location, they still remembered the Nameless King as their God of the Sun. As the early inhabitants of Lothric found themselves facing large numbers of wyverns, they had to become dragonslayers to survive; and so they turned to the Nameless King, building an altar for him. The first knights of Lothric devoted themselves to the worship of the ancestral deity of the sun and war, who in return gave them the tools to face the wyverns. Their first armors were heavy masses of iron capable of withstanding dragon fire and similar in design to the ancient armor of the dragonslayers of Anor Londo, while their shields were capable of absorbing the fierce lightning attacks of wyverns. Archdragon Peak is populated by Man Serpents and Rock Lizards. It was seemingly built as a shrine to worship the Ancient Dragons by their descendants, the Man Serpents. Contrary to what its name implies, this area does not currently contain any true dragons, as those died long ago at the hands of the first Lords. snippet: From the day the king returned from his incursion into the land of the Giants, a dark shadow had gradually covered his expression, with even his vassals noticing a change in his character. title: Shira, Knight of Filianore
snippet: Shira would eventually have to quell a corruption that had been growing within the very city, caused by a mad king that had emerged among the other Pygmy Lords. When she tried to put him to rest, she realized that his body could not die, and he simply remained impaled to her cross spear, which began to be permeated with the king's dark power. As a result, Shira would bring her weapon to a darkroom, sealing the door shut and remaining by its side to ensure the king would remain put. Even in this prolonged captivity, the descendant of the Gods remained dignified, wearing her noble attire even though no one would see it.

title: The Old Chaos
snippet: The king made some attempts to combat the Chaos, and his knights delved valiantly into the depths to exterminate the terrible things that dwelled there, but not one of them returned. title: Dragon
snippet:
The Nameless King is referenced to have sided with the Dragons and is speculated to be the first-born son of Gwyn, indicated by several descriptions on weapons and his boss soul. He is referenced as a dragon-slaying god of war who sacrificed everything to side with the Dragons, and Gwyn's first-born son is said to have been stripped of his stature as punishment for his foolishness and effectively removed from history as a result. When encountered, he is riding a Stormdrake, named King of the Storm.

Darkeater Midir is the only remaining dragon encountered in *Dark Souls III: The Ringed City.* Raised by the Gods of Lordran themselves to combat the growing Abyss, Midir's everlasting battle against the darkness has taken its toll on him, and he is slowly being consumed by the dark's influence. Fearing that the darkness within him may drive him mad, the Ashen One is tasked by Shira to put him down before he is lost to the Abyss.

The sword used by the Four Kings was intended to be in the game, however, it was removed from the final version of the game.
The Four Kings are the only holders of a Lord Soul or Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard that are not shown in the opening cinematic.
The name of the boss may reference a group of 1980s boxing legends also known as the Four Kings. One of them, Sugar Ray Leonard, is referenced in the Rayleonard Corporation of *Armored Core 4* and *For Answer*. Ironically, however, the Four Kings are weaker when at close range.

He left the Looking Glass Knight behind him, ready to expunge those who would challenge him, forever true to his original command, as the first line of defense against those who would attempt to pursue the runaway king into the Undead Crypt. The king took with him only a handful of Royal Soldiers and the faithful Sir Velstadt, and found refuge in the Shrine of Amana. Vendrick was initially intent on reaching the Throne of Want and link the First Flame but in the end the king understood that if he did so, Nashandra would have gained an easy access to the throne connected to the Flame. Vendrick thus decided to free himself from his soul, abandoning it among the ruins, to descend even deeper into the Undead Crypt. Here, left alone, he isolated himself in a secluded room wearing only his robes, crown, sword and his ring. Overcome by nihilism, Vendrick was consumed by the curse and soon

title: Ancient Dragon
snippet: Rumors abound in Drangleic about the king's brother, Lord Aldia, who tried to create a dragon. Perhaps the existence of the Ancient Dragon, and its dubious origins, are testament to his success.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
The Bearer of the Curse will journey through the Black Gulch to find the fallen kingdom of Shulva, Sanctum City, once ruled by the Sunken King. The king ruled the city, centred around the worship of a slumbering dragon known as Sinh, until his kingdom was invaded by the Drakeblood Knights lead by Sir Yorgh, who sought to claim the dragon's blood. Sir Yorgh slew the king, and awoke the dragon, which proceeded to kill him and lay waste to the city with its poison. The Bearer of the Curse slays Elana, the Squalid Queen, a child of the Abyss, and the dragon Sinh to claim the Sunken King's crown.

Next, the Bearer of the Curse returns to the Old Iron Kingdom, to seek the Old Iron King's crown. Finding the kingdom under the sway of another child of the Abyss, Nadalia, Bride of Ash, the Bearer braves their way through the ruined towers to find the Fume Knight, who guards the crown of the Old Iron King.

snippet:
Crown of the Ivory King (helm) -  Dark Souls II - armor - description 
 description : Crown of the Ivory King who once ruled this land.

Far to the north, a King built a great cathedral to appease the raging flame. But when he sensed the degradation of his soul, he left without a word, leaving everything to Alsanna, who had, unbeknownst, found a place at his side.

But these were events of long ago, and today, no one even remembers the King's name.

title: Lothric
snippet: the state of his kingdom to protect the "child of dragons", the culmination of his desires and the only thing left in his life. Despite his efforts, the king was not even able to see Ocelotte, merely holding him tightly in his palm. Moreover, the secrets of the moonlight, central to his frenzied search, eluded him in the end.

title: Burnt Ivory King
snippet:
At an unknown point, an ancient Chaos was discovered deep below the land. Legend holds that the Ivory King used his magnificent soul to build Eleum Loyce and contain the spread of Chaos. A grand cathedral was built in an attempt to appease the raging flame, but the Chaos would not be sated. As a precaution, various knights and golems were posted throughout the Garrison Ward to lead the advance on the swollen flame on his orders. Other knights were ordered to delve into the depths of Chaos to exterminate the terrible things that dwelt there, but not one of the knights returned.

Eventually, the Ivory King sensed the degradation of his soul and left Eleum Loyce without a word, leaving everything to Alsanna. He traveled deep into the Chaos until he and his knights were corrupted by the flames. At some point after the King's departure, the ivory gates of the city were flung open, and the land grew cold and lifeless.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Centuries after the end of Vendrick's reign, Drangleic would be known in Lothric as "Drang", the land of the legend of the Linking of the Fire. Vendrick's name has been lost to history, who is remembered only as the "Old King of Want", an ancient ruler that was cursed by an all-consuming thirst, making him no king at all in the end. The Dragonriders of his royal guard and their immense strength are also properly remembered. A group of soldiers, who proclaimed themselves descendants of Drangleic and wore the geisteel armor made by the blacksmith of Vendrick's Castle, abandoned the region and became sellswords. Known as Drang Knights, they scattered across the lands and quickly became known for shieldless, aggressive fighting tactics that utilized twinspears and hammers, striking fear into the hearts of their enemies.

title: Frozen Eleum Loyce
snippet:
In addition the Ivory King was served by seven beasts infused with wondrous souls and each of them were conferred a specific duty. Aava became the guardian of Alsanna as the King's beloved child while Lud and Zallen were tasked with the mercy killing of exiles

However the flames of Chaos would not be sated and the Ivory King was forced to use the power of his own soul to keep it at bay. Over time he was drained of his vigour and when he sensed the degradation of his power he decided to plunge into Chaos' heart in an attempt to reduce its flames alone. He decided to leave without a word to his subjects and left everything to Alsanna who had now found her place at his side, conferring a sword inscribed with the name of the land to her. In the end, despite the remnants of his strong soul, even the Ivory King lost the battle against Chaos and was devoured by its flames, becoming an empty husk controlled by them.

title: Nashandra
snippet: When Drangleic was ravaged by the second war with the giants and the spread of the Undead Curse, Vendrick came to realize the true nature and identity of Nashandra, and what she had coveted all along. Knowing that his time was short and that his queen had to be stopped, Vendrick created several impasses that would prevent Nashandra from seizing the throne, and sealed himself away in the Undead Crypt. This left Nashandra the sole ruler of Drangleic, albeit without much left to rule at all, as the kingdom had been all but destroyed.

title: Oceiros, the Consumed King
snippet: In his later years, frustrated by continuous failures to find a worthy Champion, Oceiros was driven to insanity by his work with Lothric's blood and became fascinated with dragons and sought other means of achieving his goal. Eventually, Oceiros turned to the cursed knowledge of the Grand Archives, where he found the twisted worship of Seath, developing a fascination for the Pale Dragon, his mad research and the secrets of his moonlight. His newfound devotion was testified by his dragonscale ring, which he claimed protected him from his enemies, and his army's usage of shields decorated with a white dragon. His fascination soon became obsession, which progressed to insanity. The loss of his sanity in the pursuit of the ways of the White Dragon would earn him the name "Consumed King" and many assassins were sent to remove the king from power, none of whom succeeded, owing according to Oceiros to the divine protection of his dragonscale ring.

title: Old Iron King
snippet: pyromancer who wanted to breath life into fire. At the height of his power, the Iron King was known for his arrogance and indulgency in hedonism, mining so intensely parts of his kingdom that poison leaked from the earth, It was at this moment that Sir Alonne left the king's service and set off to unknown lands. At some point, the Old Iron Kingdom was afflicted by the Curse of the Undead. The Old Iron King imprisoned the undead in the Huntsman's Copse, torturing them and personally presiding over so-called "undead hunts" with his best men, as well as creating the Executioner's Chariot to torture the undead eternally. He later gave the Huntsman's Copse to his Skeleton Lords.

title: Four Kings
snippet: Having failed to eliminate the dark threat, an agonizing and terrible decision was made: flooding the entire land of New Londo despite the realization that countless lives and the rich culture of the country would be lost. For this task, sorcerers were called, and the feat was accomplished without even evacuating the city's civilians, sealing away the Four Kings, their Darkwraiths and the entire population with them. The victims were thus cursed, and became Ghosts roaming the ruins of their country, seeking to make mincemeat of every living being.

title: Four Kings
snippet:
Four Kings -  Dark Souls - boss - lore 
 lore : The Four Kings were once the great leaders of a country of humans. During the Age of Fire, Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight recognized their abilities and foresight and rewarded them with a fragment of his powerful Lord Soul and the title of kings, using his power to bind and hold close to him the powerful humans. The god also allowed them to build their civilization of New Londo near Anor Londo as a lower vassal of the city of the gods. Over time their city of humans grew to host countless lives, becoming a robust and flourishing culture. Although at some point the First Flame began to fade out, leading to the emergence of the Curse of Undeath, the city continued to exist and function as an Undead city, implying the good governance of the four kings who managed to adapt to the change.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Initially the king took over the existing structures that had helped contain the curse under previous countries such as the Lost Bastille and the No-man's Wharf, using the golems and creatures already present such as the Flexile Sentries and the Ruin Sentinels as jailers. Undead Citizens of the kingdom who died and returned to life cursed would thus be locked in the squalid fortress and, once the numbers swelled to fill the cells, forced inside rickety ships and sent to certain death in the open sea. But the ongoing conflict and the resulting increase in deaths would only lead to more undead and more hollows. In an attempt to stave off the curse of undeath that was plaguing his kingdom, Vendrick hired some deserted members of the shadow knights from Mirrah, skilled assassins, to put down the hollows, making them work in the No-man's Wharf where they sent the imprisoned undead to die in the sea, but before long they became hollow themselves. More and more desperate, Vendrick came to

title: Nashandra
snippet: Left without a king and with no means to claim the Throne of Want, Nashandra’s plans were stalled until the arrival of the Bearer of the Curse, an undead powerful enough to defeat the Four Old Ones and gain access to Drangleic Castle. Nashandra manipulated the Bearer of the Curse into opening the way to the Throne of Want by aiding them in seizing the Throne of Want. She directs the Bearer of the Curse toward the Undead Crypt, suggesting that they put an end to the now-hollowed King Vendrick and claim his ring. She then directs the Bearer of the Curse to journey to Aldia's Keep to acquire the Ashen Mist Heart, and warns them that the Ancient Dragon there is no more than a prop and a false deity. At last, she directs the Bearer of the Curse toward the Forest of Fallen Giants to visit the memories of the Giants and obtain the last key to the Throne: the Giant's Kinship.

snippet: The Scholar alludes to the fates of the three kings, whether or not the player has played through *The Lost Crowns* DLCs. title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet: Seeking vengeance for the subjugation of his kingdom, the king of the Giants amassed an army in a vengeful counter-invasion of Drangleic. He also sought to reclaim the invaluable "prize" stolen from him. Unwilling to forgive the actions of Vendrick, the Giants crossed the sea and landed on the northern shores of Drangleic. They set siege to Drangleic Castle and relentlessly attacked various settlements, forts and keeps across the land for several generations.

title: Frozen Eleum Loyce
snippet: After their King was consumed by Chaos, many of Eleum Loyce's faithful knights decided to follow him and put him out of his misery, as his orders were to eliminate each malformed terror that arose from the flame, and they would thus not hesitate even it were their own leader. Sir Fabian led the loyal knights straight into the depths of the Old Chaos to exterminate its terrors one last time, however the mission proved to be a failure and not one of the selfless knights returned. The souls of the knights were taken by Chaos and corrupted, leading them to lose all sense of purpose and being, left in them driven only by the urge of expuning any who might disturb the flames, even if they were former compatriots. With their armor charred and burnt black by fire and still burning in agony they remained as empty shells controlled by the Chaos alongside their once-proud king. However a few woeful suls were able to sneak back home guided by the last faint vestige of self.

snippet:

 about_their_place_in_the_world : It's possible that the Divine Blacksmiths were worshippers or even direct followers of the Nameless Blacksmith Deity, and that their statues depict them praying to the god.

As the gods' original blacksmith, it's also likely that they worked on or oversaw the production of many of the armors, weapons, and other various equipment used by the pantheon and their followers. The unique flower design featured on the armors of Smough, Gwyn, and even the Crystal General, could potentially be traced back to them, though it might just be a general symbol of the royal family of Anor Londo, in reference to the chrysanthemum being a symbol of the Japanese Imperial Family.

snippet: fire of souls was not enough to harness the curse, and how the Flame would soon fade and the souls of ancient beings would reemerge, before Dark would descend as a curse on humans, making them take their true, immortal form. With the fire extinguished men would finally regain their true form and bury the shackles that the gods imposed on them. Yet he continued to look for an alternative, a way to maintain the world and life as it had always been, frightened by a future of Dark. As the kingdom was on the verge of being overwhelmed by the Giant Lord's offensive, King Vendrick disappeared. As every last attempt to purge the curse of Undeath had failed, he understood that the only solution available was to link the Fire himself, sacrificing his immense soul to temporarily eliminate the undead curse and give a glimmer of hope to his ruined kingdom.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Finally, the Bearer of the Curse travels to Frozen Eleum Loyce, once ruled by the Ivory King. Built to contain the Old Chaos, the city was abandoned and froze over when its king vanished into the chaos. Guided by the last child of the Abyss, Alsanna, Silent Oracle, the Bearer of the Curse seeks out the remaining knights of Eleum Loyce to gain their help in braving the Old Chaos. Finding the Burnt Ivory King there, the Bearer of the Curse defeats him and claims his crown.

Once the Bearer of the Curse has found all three crowns of old, along with Vendrick's own crown, the fallen king will unleash the hidden power of the crowns, making the Bearer of the Curse immune to the hollowing effects of the curse. Bidding the Bearer to seek strength, and asking them whether allowing the flames to fade is truly their only choice, the king sends the Bearer of the Curse on their way.

snippet:

When the First Flame began to fade and the time came for Prince Lothric to fulfill his destiny and become a Lord of Cinder, he refused the call. After reflecting on his mentor's teachings, the state of the kingdom and the world, his accursed life, and the atrocities committed for the Flame, the prince denounced the legacy of the Lords, and chose to await the Flame's death from the distance. Unable and unwilling to fulfill their destiny, the princes retreated to their chambers atop Lothric Castle to await the end of the world, protected by their royal guard and Lion Knight Albert, Black Hand Kamui and Daughter of Crystal Kriemhild.

title: Dragon Slayer Ornstein
snippet: Together, these two powerful warriors would become the last ritual challenge before a Chosen Undead could be rewarded with the Lordvessel. Only after a lethal and lengthy trial, which involved ringing the Bells of Awakening and surviving Sen's Fortress, could the Chosen Undead be granted entry into the city of the gods. Here, guarding the chambers of Gwynevere, Ornstein waited alongside Smough, and oversaw those seeking an audience with the Princess of Sunlight. However, after centuries of waiting for the Chosen Undead without success, Ornstein grew tired of his duty, and left the cathedral under his companion's watch, to search for the Nameless King, while leaving behind the ring that symbolized his membership in the Four Knights of Gwyn. Ornstein's ring was preserved as a relic by Dark Sun Gwyndolin and protected in his manor when Irithyll of the Boreal Valley rose from the ruins of Anor Londo.

title: Drangleic
snippet: As the war dragged on, Vendrick's army began a decline caused by attrition in the face of the Giants' will of steel. The king was forced to hire mercenaries from Forossa and Volgen to reinforce his ranks, and Desert Sorceresses from Jugo were added to the defense of the Royal Castle. The endless battles also began to take their toll on the population. Those who could afford it ran away to other countries while the poor were left without a place to sleep, the kingdom now reduced to ruins. The conflict continued for three generations unabated, with the Giants sustaining their attacks on northern fortifications and trying to push their way inland towards the Royal Castle. The bodies of the many dead giants that littered the region slowly grew into great trees, covering the area around Cardinal Tower in a dense forest.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Thanks to this discovery Vendrick became the monarch who came closest to becoming a true "King" and turning his wants into reality. He had access to the primordial Flame whose power could decide the fate of the world, either by linking it to prolong the state of the world or refusing this fate and leading the world to darkness as a Dark Lord. Vendrick, however, never made either decision and continued to reign over Drangleic. Both he and his brother were not convinced by the two possible choices and, anchored to the illusion of the form that life had during the Age of Fire, they looked for a way to maintain it, searching for a way to free humans from the curse of Undeath and breaking the seal of fire that imprisoned them. As he deepened his knowledge of souls and curses, Vendrick effectively reigned over Drangleic, protecting the country from any external threats. Nashandra helped bring peace to the kingdom, a peace so profound that it reminded humans of the Dark from which they came.

title: Old Iron King
snippet: The Iron King would at some point trying to control the soul residing into the lava where the Iron Keep was built. He therefore immersed the Smelter Demon in the lava trying to infuse it with the soul lurking beneath, but when the iron golem was possessed, it struck down the king, and the lava raged sunking the Iron Keep. The King was then possessed by the evil that lurked below the magma, and his body then became molten earth.

title: Northern Sea
snippet: During his reign, King Vendrick was advised by Queen Nashandra that across the sea there was the looming thretat of the Giants. Vendrick gathered an army and crossed the ocean, defeated the Giants, pillaged their land and took control of their great power, using it to create the golems and further develop his kingdom. However, the giants, angered by the invasion and barbarism of the king of Drangleic, responded by crossing the sea and directly invading the human kingdom with the desire to take revenge on Vendrick, bringing war that consumed Drangleic for centuries with their directed and burning rage..

title: Olaphis
snippet: The kingdom of Olaphis soon fell to the curse, most of its population turned undead or hollow and others perished in the mad purges of the king. Traces of Olaphis culture remained in the region through history. The "Lost" Bastille became the stronghold of the kingdom of Venn, where the Belfry Luna of the princess was built and defended by Belfry Gargoyles, while the Kingdom of Alken was able to recover the Flame Swathe pyromancy of Straid. Some of the wise men who survived the purges of the king and the desperate sea voyage, reaching the south, imparted their knowledge of sorcery and pyromancy to the land where they ended up. Olenford in particular became revered as the father of sorcery in the country that they would help found and that would become known by the name of Melfia. Much later King Vendrick and his brother Aldia conducted research on Olaphis, managing to rediscover Straid's sorceries like Soul Bolt.

The Pursuer already drops the Mad Knight's rings upon defeat, but he also has a separate connection to Venn and Alken from his spawn locations at Lost Bastille and Iron Keep, which were once part of both vanished kingdoms.

snippet:
Archdragon Peak -  Dark Souls III - location - trivia 
 trivia : This area draws heavily upon Byzantine architecture as inspiration for its appearance and design. The building that serves as the Dragon-Kin Mausoleum, in particular, bears a striking resemblance to churches (and mosques) designed in Byzantine tradition, the most famous icon of which is [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hagia_Sophia Hagia Sophia] in Istanbul, Turkey.
** Interestingly, it is possible that the architects of Hagia Sophia considered it the sacred ground of the *demiurge*—specifically, one that manifested through light and the sun. In the Neoplatonic school, the deific figure *demiurge* is the "fashioner" of the universal order, generally held to be distinct from "*the One*" which is the essential *form* of existence. These conceptions roughly parallel the Nameless King/Gwyn and the First Flame: the Chief Gods (the demiurge) sculpted the Age of Fire from Disparity (the One).

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: Gwyndolin thus continued to remain hidden in his father's empty mausoleum, administering Anor Londo from the shadows and continuing to carry out his father's will to uphold the Age of Fire, punishing sinners and leading the Undead without revealing himself. snippet:
Both the Orb and Arrow Spread attacks are avoidable by hiding behind one of the pillars on either side of the corridor. The Sphere Shot, on the other hand, will go through walls, inflicting full damage if not blocked or avoided. The Orb Spread and Sphere Shot are Magic-based, though, so a shield that can block 100% physical damage and has good Magic resistance, like the Crest Shield, is recommended for this fight.

While devastating, both the Sphere Shot and Arrow Spread attacks have no tracking whatsoever and are easily avoided simply by running diagonally. If a player does not want to risk it too much, a good strategy to catch up to him is by moving from pillar to pillar until they are about two pillars away from Gwyndolin and then wait until he shoots his Arrow Spread. This attack can consist of two-to-four arrow barrages. Wait until he finishes the second one and go for him, if he shoots any subsequent arrows, dodge them by running diagonally.

 lead : , also known as **Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight** and **Lord Gwyn** is a character in *Dark Souls* and the final boss of *Dark Souls*.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Gwyn proved himself a skilled ruler, using his power to bind and hold close to him the potential powers of the world. He amply rewarded the betrayal of the dragon Seath and his indispensable contribution to the war, giving him the title of Duke and inducting him into the nobility of the gods through a marriage to one of his daughters. Gwyn also gave him a fragment of his powerful Lord Soul along with the Archives, and left him to his studies near Anor Londo. As for humans, cognizant of the abilities of four of their great leaders, Gwyn bequeathed on them another shard of his powerful Soul, and let them build their civilization of New Londo near the divine capital. Gwyn would also befriend the Primordial Serpent Frampt and convince him of his ideals and vision of the Age of Fire..

Despite these precautions, Gwyn continued to fear humans and the potential of their soul; so he "marked" their Dark Soul and bodies using the Flame with the Darksign, a literal ring of fire—powered by the First Flame—around the Dark Soul of humans. title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: It may be hard for the player to find a proper opening to fight back or heal as a result of Gwyn actively seeking the player. Despite his very weakened state, he is still the former Lord of Sunlight, so don't rely on lightning as he is immune. His attacks deal a great amount of damage if they connect. If blocked, his attacks will still deal considerable damage to the player as a result of the flame damage his sword deals. A good way to reduce the damage to a slight margin is by using shields with high fire defense, such as the Black Iron Greatshield or the Black Knight Shield, which can be dropped by the nearby Black Knights; however, care should still be taken as blocking a full attack chain will cost a lot of stamina and may eventually result in losing health or dying. The Gold-Hemmed Black Set can further negate the fire damage at the cost of less physical defense against his attacks.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Once his army had been prepared and armed with spears and greatbows that used arrows as big as iron spears, Gwyn went to the surface with the intention of waging war against the Dragons and conquering the world with his Lord allies. The war turned out to be very bloody; for each of the majestic creatures slain, three scores of Gwyn's soldiers perished. The bodies of dragons were harder than stone, and resistant to fire and magic, making their killing difficult. At one point Gwyn was even forced to integrate into his ranks the primordial humans, descendants of the Furtive Pygmy who had found the Dark Soul, and who had developed their own weapons and armor infused with the life-giving power of the Abyss.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet:
Gwyn, Lord of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Gwyn is one of the primordial humanoid creatures that appeared underground after the First Flame appeared, bringing life, death and disparity. He was among those who found the four Lord Souls, sources of immense power, together with Gravelord Nito, the Witch of Izalith and the Furtive Pygmy.

With the immense power of his soul, the greatest among all the Lords, Gwyn established an underground civilization, becoming its ruler and forming an army of Silver Knights. At some point Gwyn had a relationship with an unknown woman and from their union were born his firstborn son and his eldest daughter, Gwynevere.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet:
Gwyn, Lord of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Gwyn's title uses the kanji "薪の王" that can be literally translated as "King of Kindling" or "King of Firewood".
Gwyn's design and lore seems to have been heavily inspired by Zeus of ancient Greek mythology.
Several aspects of him can also be compared to the Welsh deity Gwyn ap Nudd.
**Gwyn ap Nudd is said to be a warrior with a "blackened face" similar to Gwyn's hollowed flesh, and the King of the "fair folk." The gods of Lordran being a fair folk.
**In Arthurian legends and writings, Gwyn ap Nudd was the ruler of a delightful paradise called the otherworld, or Annwn. Such a place would be similar to Anor Londo during its glory days.
**Additionally, one can make a comparison between Gwyn ap Nudd leading the Wild Hunt in Welsh legend, and the dragon hunts of Gwyn.
"Gwyn" translated from Welsh means "White/Pure" or "Holy".

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet:
The pillars in the arena can be used to block his attacks, however, Gwyn will easily move around them and continue attacking. It is possible for him to keep attacking a pillar that is blocking his path, giving the player a chance to heal, however, he may simply go around it.

Parrying is a high-risk, but incredibly efficient strategy. All of Gwyn's attacks, minus the kick and grab, can be parried. Using the Hornet Ring, a single riposte can erase a large fraction of Gwyn's health. However, any mistakes can end up badly for the player. Therefore, it may be preferable to opt for heavier armor for this strategy, as dodging is not the main tactic, and the additional poise and defense leaves some margin for error. It is ideal to block the first hit of his combo, and parry the telegraphed second hit. After performing a riposte, the player will have just enough time to Estus heal.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin at some point learned of Gwyn's existence and his story but not his name, referring to him merely as the "Lord of Light". He understood how Gwyn altered the natural order and began linking the Flame, which extended the Age of Fire against the course of nature, and he expresses his outrage at Gwyn for making men lesser than their original form as the "Lord of Light" banished Dark and all that stemmed from Humanity with the Darksign, defining it as the "First Sin" committed against humans and their nature.

snippet: Gwyn would also establish the order of his Four Knights, chosen amongst his most trusted warriors, and entrust them with several vital tasks along with their own special souls. Dragonslayer Ornstein was (likely) named captain of the order, with Hawkeye Gough leading the Dragonslayers and Greatarchers, Artorias leading the Knights and Ciaran leading the Lord's Blades, an order of female assassins tasked with eliminating Gwyn's enemies from the shadows.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: At one point, the Witch of Izalith used her Lord Soul in an attempt to replicate the generative properties of the First Flame, resulting in her producing a Flame of Chaos and transforming herself into a Bed of Chaos that began producing Demons. Izalith and her daughters would eventually bring the Flame of Chaos under their control, and learn how to use it, moving from being fire sorcerers to developing pyromancy and creating a new society together with the demons generated by the Bed of Chaos.  dark_souls_iii : The remnants of the will and power of Gwyn, as the first one to ever link the First Flame, would emerge as part of the Soul of Cinder, the deific manifestation of the souls of all those who have linked themselves to the First Flame throughout history, thus creating a hollowed-out entity possessing all the abilities of the previous Champions.

The powers of Gwyn would manifest when the Soul of Cinder was challenged by an aspiring Champion; acting as the Flame's last line of defense within the Kiln, the Soul of Cinder fought to either test the might of one who would link the Flame, or to protect it from a would-be betrayer or usurper.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Now bereft of most of his Lord Soul's power and with only the power of his soul, Gwyn left for the Kiln of the First Flame, the structure built to house and protect it, with only his robes, his mighty greatsword and his powerless crown, accompanied only by a guard of Black Knights. Eventually Gwyn linked the First Flame, prolonging its life but himself being consumed by it, reduced to the empty husk of cinders guarding the core of the Kiln. The inferno of the newly kindled fire melted the surroundings and burned his knights to ashes, leaving them to wander the world as disembodied spirits.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet:
Gwyn, Lord of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategies 
 strategies : Health and Stamina management are a must in this fight, as Gwyn will rarely give the player any chances to heal. Because of this, Elizabeth's Mushroom is an essential healing item for this fight as it continuously restores health over a 30 second time frame and can be used before the battle commences. It is heavily advisable to use a fast weapon to attack with, preferably one that drains little stamina. Heavy weapons are not recommended for this fight.
